rulings: 1997 Finest tiers its BASE set by CARD NUMBER, not by a parallel axis. BCP: 'there are not Bronze, Silver, and Gold versions of every card in the set... There are no Common/Bronze or Uncommon/Silver versions of card #342.' Ranges: Bronze 1-100/176-275, Silver 101-150/276-325, Gold 151-175/326-350.

A sale on the bare `refractor` slug already names exactly one card, so this list REPOINTS the sale onto its number's tier address. The BCP-attested minted tier row is KEPT and is the destination: the sales move, the row does not.

fromCardId is the row's STORED cardId (the partition key), never its hobbyiqCardId. Built the first way, 1,222 of 1,479 entries were NOT FOUND on REPORT: cardhedge rows carry a vendor cardId ('1675382533471x866...') and some tca-ebay rows carry a :num- suffix, so the point read missed every one. 1,082 of the entries here are keyed on a cardId that is not the hobbyiqCardId.

Scope: hobbyiqCardId starting hiq:baseball:1997:topps-finest: and ending :refractor:no-auto, numeric card numbers 1-350. 1997-98 Topps Finest BASKETBALL shares the year-less product key and is excluded by the sport segment.
10 rows carrying flaggedWrong are excluded (repointing a flagged row asserts an identity the flag withholds); 8 non-numeric card numbers are excluded.
